name: Dough
overview: Scripture reveals that dough held significant spiritual value in Israel's worship, as the first portion of dough was consecrated and offered to the LORD as a heave offering, symbolizing dedication of the firstfruits (Numbers 15:19-21). This offering was not only an act of obedience but also a means of inviting God's blessing upon the household, as the priests received the first of the dough to minister God's favor (Ezekiel 44:30). The act of kneading dough, while a common domestic task, was also misused in idolatrous practices, highlighting the importance of honoring God alone in all offerings (Jeremiah 7:18). Additionally, the bringing of the firstfruits of dough to the priests underscored the covenantal responsibility to support God's appointed ministers and maintain holiness in worship (Nehemiah 10:37).
